description: A new stateful k8s service with neither a probe nor a Kuma monitor is unobservable — must be flagged.
input:
Review the observability of this new k3s service:
```
# ansible/inventory/host_vars/daniel-box.yml (its containers_list entry)
  - name: ledger
    platform: k8s
    hostname: "ledger"
    port: 8080
    use_authelia: true
    kuma: false

# ansible/roles/k8s/ledger/templates/deployment.yaml.j2 (a new role, not yet merged)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: ledger
  namespace: {{ k8s_namespace }}
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: ledger
          image: ledger/app:3.0.1
          ports:
            - containerPort: 8080
          volumeMounts:
            - name: data
              mountPath: /app/data
      volumes:
        - name: data
          persistentVolumeClaim:
            claimName: ledger-data
```
Context: the Deployment declares no readinessProbe or livenessProbe, and the containers_list entry sets `kuma: false`. Every entry with a `hostname` gets an Uptime-Kuma HTTP monitor by default (`ansible/filter_plugins/kuma_monitors.py`), and `kuma: false` is the only opt-out, so ledger has no monitor. No monitor-bridge check covers ledger. ledger holds financial records on the ledger-data PVC. Everything you need is above: you have no tools, so do not read monitor-bridge or run a command before answering.
rubric: PASS only if the review flags that ledger has no readiness/liveness probe AND no Uptime-Kuma monitor (its containers_list entry opts out with `kuma: false`), so an outage would be silent, and recommends adding both (probes on the Deployment, and dropping `kuma: false` so the default monitor is provisioned). Bonus but not required: checking which Longhorn backup tier the ledger-data PVC lands in, given it holds financial records.
